Copied candidate rows and immutable original bytes enter a detached store. Full existing replay, reducer, descriptor, extraction and source validation runs before the final proof; missing originals cannot fall back to raw SQL.

One fresh atomic SELECT snapshot certifies standard journal/source schemas and typed all-column ordered complete-roster byte roots. Confirmed mismatch returns without installing caches; malformed or uncertain proofs propagate without retry.
The native post-validation hook checks frozen journal bytes again; live caches are installed only after a pristine recheck under live summary/source locks. No caller-owned dictionaries are installed.

Every later public read retains the existing fresh complete proof. Missing seed retains the existing cold startup; stale seed can fall back only after confirmed mismatch. Corrupt/checksum/release failures do not establish readiness.

Exporter uses bounded native metadata and 32 KiB BLOB slices, reassembles bytes before strict UTF8 decoding, checks complete source chunk rosters before payload reads and pins initial schema identities in the final atomic proof.

Exporter protocol permits execute/close only, with transaction verbs or native SELECT-only stacked-statement checks; SQL text is internally generated and source identities remain bound parameters. No journal, work-store, lease or schema initializer is constructed by export.
Artifact output stays outside Git and Sites. Only the exact server-side package-data filename is added; actual private upload construction and inspection remain with Mac.
